answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 13% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the bridge balance is debited each close, the haven ledger shows the bleed, and the wharf audit lists every fee. An operator holding 233 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
